refquickresult:
It first prints its self-tests (in the test of Section 2.3: `analytic k = 0 spectra: max error 2.181e-07`), the closed shells (`N_mid = 112, N_big = 1016, N_mid(m = 3) = 112`) and its own coupling for $(m,L,N)=(1,3,8)$, then the iterations of the four quick runs (`m1_L3_N8_lam0_T0`, `m1_L3_N8_lamp1_T0`, `m1_L3_N8_lam0_T0p3` and the single-parity run `L2-free-N8-p-1`), and ends with a line of the form

```text
wrote build/my-reference-quick/reference-summary.json in 66.3 s (4 runs, failed: [])
```

The quick grids are coarse ($N_0=30$, 60), so its numbers agree with the canonical ones only to a few digits (for example the KS gap of $N=8$, $0.4307405$ on the quick grids against $0.4307337$); the quick mode tests the program, not the results. The gate checks that the quick summary is complete, that the self-tests are present and that every run converged.
theoryresult: It prints `check_count=157` and `failed_check_count=0` and the time spent per family of checks; building the exchange table takes most of the time (167.5 s of 219.7 s in the test of Section 2.3, on a loaded two-core computer; the gate header records 171 s and 50 s for the whole checker on the 24-core computer under different loads). On the computer that produced the committed files (Windows, Python 3.14.5, numpy 2.4.6) the report and the table are reproduced byte for byte. With other versions of Python and numpy (Python 3.13 with numpy 2.5.3 in the Linux test) all 157 checks pass and the two files differ only in round-off: one recorded maximum deviation ($7.8\times10^{-15}$ instead of $5.1\times10^{-15}$) and the last digits of the quadrature error estimates of the table. The gate accepts such files value by value (relative $10^{-9}$, absolute $10^{-12}$) and logs which rule matched.
